# ELEMENTS OF A CDSS ADVICE MENU

Advice menus are comprised of the following elements:

---

# TYPICALLY present on an advice menu

---

1) Diagnosis or condition label-at the top of each advice menu.
2) Treatment. Empirical treatment as well as treatment for selected pathogens is presented with links to antimicrobial quick orders unless stated otherwise.

In addition to the drug, dose, and route, each quick order text includes the drug's approximate cost per day and coding for important drug properties of note. Drugs clustered together are considered equivalent.

3) Help. At the top of each advice menu. There are links to a variety of resources (susceptibilities, important drug properties, section-specific consults, etc.).
4) References. At the bottom on each advice menu. These are key references for the recommendations on the menu.

---

# DISCRETIONARY advice menu components

---

1) (Treatment) Alternative. Following the (preferred) Treatment section with quick orders for common alternative antimicrobials. Antimicrobial listed under each alternative header are equivalents among those listed. A broader selection of medications can be accessed through the Need an alternative menu within the help section. For some conditions we recommend alternative antimicrobials when recommended drugs are not suitable for an individual patient. Unless otherwise stated drugs clustered together under Alternatives are considered equivalent.

If none of the recommended or alternative drugs is suitable you can find more drugs by clicking on the Need an alternative link at the top of the menu.

2) Consults. At the top of the menu, these are consultation requests pertinent to the clinical problem addressed by the menu. Links to context-specific consults can be found on advice menus, as appropriate. For example, the herpes simplex encephalitis menu contains a link to a request for neurology consult.
3) Resources. Pertinent to the clinical problem and addressed by the menu is provided for example. For some menus, supplemental resources have been identified (e.g., PORT score calculator for Community Acquired Pneumonia, diagnostic tools, Epidemiology, etc.) the information is included on the advice menu.
